chapter_theme: Four songs at Ettikudi (எட்டிகுடி), one of which names Kanjirangudi: the poet confesses abandoning penance for women's breasts, being ruined and made poor by desire, and wandering in shameless lust, and asks for the teaching of Om and for the Lord's mark on him; the praise names Murugan the master of three Tamils and lists his shrines.
structure_note: 831, 833 and 834 are confessions of desire; 832 is a short plea for the teaching of Om; 834 ends with a list of shrines.

831.reading: The poet describes women with breasts like twin caskets, round, soft and thrilling, burdening the waist, smeared with sandal, and asks whether, abandoning penance, he will wander, quarrelling and embracing them again and again. The praise names Murugan the dear kinsman of Kama, son of Vishnu, who raised the cock banner and fought the Asura army, who in grace speaks the three Tamils to those who love him, and the lord at Ettikudi where pearls shine in the fields.
831.nuance: சருவிச் சருவித் தழுவித் தழுவித் தவம் அற்க விடுத்து: the doubled verbs enact the repetition of desire, and penance is what it gives up. அரி புத்திர சித்தச: Kama as Vishnu's son and Murugan's cousin.

832.reading: In a short song the poet, who grieves while thinking of pleasure as his five senses run, asks Murugan to rule him by speaking Om and what follows from it. The praise names Kumaresa, whose drawn arrows struck the Suras' clan, husband of the elephant's daughter and the hunter girl, life of devotees with minds free of attachment, the six-faced lord at Kanjirangudi.
832.nuance: ப்ரணவாதி உரைத்து எந்தனை ஆள்வாய்: the teaching of Om is asked for directly. ஓம்பை றும் before it looks damaged. The song names Kanjirangudi (காஞ்சிரங்குடி), not Ettikudi, the heading it stands under.

833.reading: The poet describes women with eyes like the sea, poison, arrows, does, fish and flowers, and breasts like lotus buds, caskets and hills that pierce him, and says that, unable to leave them and craving their union, he lost his wealth, fell into poverty and ruin and sank in mind; he asks Murugan to come to him, alone and weak, and give his lotus feet in friendship. The praise names Rama, whose unstoppable arrow took the life of the wicked ten-headed king and freed the lotus-born Sita from prison, as uncle, Murugan as the eye-like son of Siva who danced in the golden hall, and Ettikudi where shells spit pearls in the fields.
833.nuance: மிடலுற்ற கலவிக்குள் உளம் நச்சி வளமற்று மிடிபட்டு மடிபட்டு: here desire leads to poverty by itself, without the courtesans' theft. கனகப் பொதுவில் நட்புடன் அடித்த சிவன்: the dance in the golden hall is that of Chidambaram.

834.reading: The poet asks of women: is the dark hair sapphire or cloud, are the eyes fish or vel, is their speech milk, syrup or honey, the face the moon, the breasts tender coconuts or Meru, the waist a thread; and as a dog who wanders crying 'chee chee' while craving their limbs and uniting shamelessly, he asks not to suffer and wander, but to have Murugan set his mark on him, look on him with grace and come on the peacock. The praise names the child whom the three-eyed Siva praised, Kama's kinsman, Vishnu's nephew, master of the three Tamils, the lamp and incomparable form, Muruga who gives liberation to devotees, lord of Viralur, Selur, Palani, Arur, Vidaikkazhi and Vayalur, the mother within every scripture, the vel of Ettikudi.
834.nuance: The catalogue is put as questions (நீலோ மாலோ, சேலோ வேலோ), as in 822. தற்பொறி வைத்து அருள்: the Lord's mark set on the poet, like the brand on a servant. எச்சுருதிக்குளும் நீயே தாயே calls Murugan the mother in all scripture. Several shrine names in lines 19 to 21 are damaged.

links.note: Both build a woman's charms as questions (மொழி பாலோ தேனோ, விழி வேலோ; சேலோ வேலோ, பாலோ பாகோ). In 822 the questions are turned to the inner light; in 834 they lead to shame and to the Lord's mark.

831 asks whether, quarrelling and embracing women again and again, he will wander having given up penance (தவம் அற்க விடுத்து உழல்வேனோ). Kural 266 says those who do tavam do their own work and the rest, caught in desire, do what is futile (அவஞ்செய்வார் ஆசையுட் பட்டு). The song places the poet on the Kural's wrong side, with the doubled verbs (சருவிச் சருவித் தழுவித் தழுவி) showing the futile repetition.

832 says the poet grieves as his five senses run (ஓங்கும் ஐம்புலன் ஓட) after pleasure and asks Murugan to rule him by speaking Om. Kural 24 says one who guards the five with the goad of firmness (உரனென்னும் தோட்டியான் ஓரைந்தும் காப்பான்) is a seed for the higher world. Where the Kural's goad is the man's own firmness, the song looks for it outside, in the guru's pranava.

833 says that craving union with women (கலவிக்குள் உளம் நச்சி) he lost his wealth and fell into poverty and ruin (வளமற்று மிடிபட்டு மடிபட்டு). Kural 920 says double-minded women, liquor and dice are the company of those Fortune has left (திருநீக்கப் பட்டார் தொடர்பு). The song tells as a sequence what the Kural states as a sign: desire first, then the loss of திரு.

834 questions the women's features in pairs of alternatives, among them whether their eyes are fish or vel (அக்கண் இணைக்கு இணை சேலோ வேலோ). Kural 1085 asks of a girl's look whether it is Death, an eye or a doe (கூற்றமோ கண்ணோ பிணையோ). Both use the same questioning form for the eye, with a weapon among the answers; the song makes the questions part of the craving it asks to be freed from.

source_issues: Song 832 names Kanjirangudi (காஞ்சிரங்குடி) in its last line, not Ettikudi, the heading it stands under.
